title: Returning trusts
hook: the night he left Mecca, the Prophet left Ali behind to give back other people's things
tomorrow: if you got one sentence at the very end, which one?

segments.voice: Yesterday: no grudge. The man of Paradise did nothing special except set it down every night. Some things you put down. Others you have to hand back.

It's night in Mecca, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is about to leave the city for good, with men plotting against him. He is taking almost no one. But he leaves someone behind on purpose: his young cousin, Ali. Tradition says Ali lay down in the Prophet's own bed that night. The reason he stayed is the surprising part. People of Mecca, including some who rejected his message, had left their valuables in the Prophet's keeping. And he wasn't leaving with a single one.
screen: `NIGHT IN MECCA.` → `ALI STAYS BEHIND.` → `OTHER PEOPLE'S VALUABLES.`

segments.voice: So Ali stayed, the early biographies say, and handed each deposit back to its owner before he followed. Notice the timing. The people getting their things back were the city that had just pushed the Prophet out. He could have called it even. He didn't. The Qur'an makes it a command, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners." The Arabic word is amanah, a trust: anything placed in your hands that belongs to someone else. A borrowed charger. A friend's secret. Money you owe. The tradition takes this seriously: a hadith in Sahih Muslim says even a martyr is forgiven everything except a debt. But it isn't meant to crush anyone. A hadith in Bukhari says whoever takes people's money meaning to pay it back, Allah will help them repay. The intention, and then the next step. Before a long trip, you return the library books. Before the longest one, the tradition says: settle what you can. Worth remembering: on the night he fled, the Prophet made sure his enemies got their things back.
screen: `ALI RETURNS EACH DEPOSIT.` · `RESTORE DEPOSITS TO THEIR OWNERS.` · `AMANAH: WHAT ISN'T YOURS.` · `INTEND, THEN TAKE A STEP.` · then, large: `ALL SETTLED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing in your hands that isn't yours: a borrowed book, a loan, a promise half-kept. If a short message would start settling it, write that message now, even if you send it later. If not, decide the very next step and when you'll take it.
screen: `ONE THING THAT ISN'T YOURS.` · `WRITE THE MESSAGE.` · `OR NAME THE NEXT STEP.`

segments.voice: Returning trusts: giving back what was placed in your hands, from a borrowed thing to a debt, so that nothing is left owing.
The line for the road: all settled, or at least the next step taken. Good night from day seven of the journey home.

howItsDone: Muslims treat debts and things held in trust (amanah) as serious duties; before travel, illness or old age, some write down what they owe and what they hold for others, and the Prophet's leaving Ali to return the Meccans' deposits is a story often told about it.
